title: Sheetwise flat-complex computation of the compactified etale coefficient arrow
statement:
Let $e:U\to V$ be a separated etale finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes and choose a compactification $U\xrightarrow jW\xrightarrow rV$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings and let $P$ be a bounded cochain complex of flat $A$-module sheaves on $U_{\rm et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use ordinary module derived categories, coefficient extension $T=-\otimes_A^L B$, and exact sum extension $e_{\Sigma!}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. The complexes $j_!P$ and $r_*j_!P$ are flat termwise and K-flat. Each term $j_!P^n$ is $r_{*,A}$-acyclic and each $j_!(P^n\otimes_A B)$ is $r_{*,B}$-acyclic; acyclic means its higher direct images vanish. The canonical acyclic-complex identifications and sheet-component normalization identify $Rr_*j_!P$ with the complex $e_{\Sigma!}P$, also after coefficient extension [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization].
Under these specified models, the coefficient map formed by the proper $B$-linear counit transpose followed by the open tensor identification is represented by the natural chain map
$$(e_{\Sigma!,A}P)\otimes_A B\longrightarrow e_{\Sigma!,B}(P\otimes_A B),\qquad (x_s)_s\otimes b\longmapsto(x_s\otimes b)_s.$$
Here each element of a direct sum has finite support; the index set of sheets may be empty. This identifies the actual counit-transpose map, not merely isomorphic endpoints, and needs no flatness of $B/A$. Flatness and K-flatness use [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Schemes and Noetherian rings use [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-etale-compactification-bounded-models] with $(R,K)=(A,P)$ and $(B,P\otimes_A B)$. The latter complex is bounded on the same interval because tensor sends zero to zero; flatness is not required for this application. This gives both families of higher-direct-image vanishings, the canonical acyclic and sheet identifications, and Noetherianity of $W$. Its flat clause for $(A,P)$ gives termwise flatness and K-flatness of $j_!P$, $r_*j_!P$ and $P$. For the independent-coefficient K-flat predicates, use the constant-module equivalence and its flatness comparison [lem-pur-etale-constant-module-flat] [lem-pur-etale-sum-tensor-test], then the bounded-above site-flat criterion [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat]. The realization equivalence is additive, so it preserves the upper bound.

proof.text: Put $C=j_!P$. Apply [lem-sp-acyclic-flat-proper-coefficient-model]: $r$ is proper, $W,V$ are Noetherian, both rings are finite, and step 1 supplies boundedness, flatness and acyclicity. For its $B$-acyclicity hypothesis identify $C\otimes_A B$ with $j_!(P\otimes_A B)$ using [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor]. The theorem represents the actual proper $B$-counit transpose by $\pi_C$, natural in chain maps. Compose with $r_*$ of the ordinary open tensor map. This represents the specified derived open map as well: both open comparisons restrict to the identity on $U$ and are maps between open extensions, so the fully faithful open adjunction identifies them [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor] [def-sp-open-coefficient-unit-iso]. The equality with the normalized derived open scalar map follows by applying the open adjunction hom-equivalence to the inverse maps and using its unit normalization [lem-pur-etale-open-scalar-exchange]. Its K-flat model equation is the q_normalized clause of [lem-coef-etale-open-scalar-coherence], also exposed by the open tensor comparisons.

proof.text: For each degree apply [lem-sp-etale-compactification-sheaf-scalar-map] to $M=P^n$. It identifies the ordinary composite of step 2 under the degree-zero sheet comparisons with $(x_s)_s\otimes b\mapsto(x_s\otimes b)_s$. Its equality of sheaf maps applies to locally constant $b$ and local finite-support generators, with no global splitting assumption. The sum isomorphism formed with the upper-star adjunction equals the one formed with literal localization restriction: compare their transposes, expand the transported units, use the scalar/restriction comparison and naturality, and cancel the restriction isomorphism. Apply the graph/scalar identity degreewise.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), expanded bounded-model calculation; Tag 0GKF (lemma-f-shriek-projection), pure-tensor rule.

proof.text: The degreewise formula is a chain map: applying either differential composite to a generator gives $(d x_s\otimes b)_s$. The canonical-model compatibility of step 1 and the natural representation of step 2 identify its localization with the named derived coefficient map [lem-sp-etale-compactification-bounded-models] [lem-sp-acyclic-flat-proper-coefficient-model]. Tensor preserves finite sums; empty sheets give $0\to0$. The same computation covers $P=0$, $A=B$ with identity map, and $B=0$. K-flat source models compute derived tensor throughout; no exactness of $-\otimes_A B$ was used. Expand the model boundary. Naturality of the proper coefficient map moves the open localization factor; the normalized open model equality, the proper model equality, scalar-representative naturality, acyclic-comparison naturality and the localized graph identity then give the displayed equation by associativity.
